name: A Wardrobe Through Time
description: Wrapped cloth, stiff collars, jeans and bikinis: what people wore and what clothes meant in different ages and places.

checkpoints.name: Wrapped and draped
checkpoints.note: The oldest clothes were lengths of cloth. Silkworms gave China its silk, cotton was woven in India for garments such as the sari, Roman citizens wore the toga, and Korean dress took shapes later seen in tomb paintings.

checkpoints.name: Robes and rules
checkpoints.note: Dress marked rank and custom. Japan developed the kimono, and in China foot binding turned a fashion for tiny feet into a painful practice that lasted for centuries among families who wanted status.

checkpoints.name: Courts and collars
checkpoints.note: European courts set fashions with corsets, ruffs, heels and neckties, while the Asante of Ghana wove kente cloth for royalty, with patterns that carried names and meanings. The spinning jenny of the 1760s sped up spinning and began to make cloth cheaper.

checkpoints.name: Hoops and rivets
checkpoints.note: Factories made cloth cheap and fashions changed faster. The sewing machine sped up tailoring, huge crinoline skirts swept through Europe and America, Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis patented riveted work trousers, and the zipper and Vogue magazine arrived in the 1890s.

checkpoints.name: The casual century
checkpoints.note: Sportswear and underwear became daily clothes. Coco Chanel made simple clothes chic, nylon gave a cheap new fibre, and T-shirts, sneakers and bikinis broke old rules. The miniskirt and the qipao showed how fashion could be a statement.
